mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.25% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where real GDP increases over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production by more than 2% over three months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where industrial production declines by more than 2% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures signals a strong demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures increase.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000 over a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and business investment improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 over a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index over three months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the consumer price index increases consistently over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real GDP and housing starts signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic activity slows and consumer confidence wanes.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where both real GDP and housing starts decline.
